sentences.text: Ms. T.H. Khan, AGP for Respondent / State  CORAM:
AVINASH G. GHAROTE, J.

DATED : 11th JULY, 2023 Heard Mr. Dhore, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. Khan,
learned AGP for respondent No.1.

None appears for the respondent Nos. 2 to 4 though served as long back as on 06/05/2022.
2.

The only contention raised by Mr. Dhore, learned counsel for the petitioner is that in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 3(5)(g) of the National Highways Act, the respondent No.1 had held one Shyamrao Kinnake (the father of the petitioner); Meerabai - respondent No. 2 and Hirabai - mother of respondent Nos.3 and 4, as joint owners of land of Gat No.143 Mouza Saoner, Tah. Ralegaon,
thereby entitling them for compensation.
This was in exercise of power under Section 3(5)(g) of the National Highways Act by way of an award dated 2 926-3953-21.odt 31/1/2019.

The objection thereafter was raised by respondent Nos. 2 and 3 on 20/6/2019 contending that the petitioner herein was not the son of Shyamrao Kinnake, which objection considering the declaration by the learned appellate Court in R.C.A. 48/2008 dated 01/4/2014 (page 37) that the petitioner is the son of Shyamrao and Sumitra Kinnake was dismissed by the order dated 13/7/2020 and it was held that in case the respondents No.2 and 3 have any grievance regarding the said order they should obtain appropriate orders from the Civil Court (page 39).

This order, has been reviewed by the competent authority respondent No.1 by the impugned order dated 20/10/2020, holding that the petitioner Suresh S/O Shyamrao Kinnake vs Sub Divisional Officer And Land ... on 11 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148197039/
1 should obtain succession certificate under the Indian Succession Act and submit it before the respondent No.1 in order to claim the share of Shyamrao Kinnake.

2. Once the respondent No.1 competent authority in exercise of power under Section 3(5)(g) of the National Highways Act holds that a claimant before him is entitled for apportionment of the claim under Section 3 (H)(iii) of the aforesaid Act which is evident from the order dated 13/7/2020 by which the objections by the respondent Nos.2 and 3, were rejected there is no power in the competent 3 926-3953-21.odt authority to review his own order.
That apart, when the appellate Court has passed the decree on 01/4/2014, declaring that the petitioner was the duly adopted son of Shyamrao Kinnake, that decree was final and conclusive.
This being the position, the impugned order dated 20/10/2020, cannot be sustained.
The same is hereby quashed and set aside.
The respondent No.1 is directed to release the share of Shyamrao Kinnake in favour of the petitioner.
The petition is allowed in the above terms.
No costs.

JUDGE MP Deshpande Suresh S/O Shyamrao Kinnake vs Sub Divisional Officer And Land ... on 11 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148197039/
